method: raw-firing examples, blind: interpreter read ONLY the firing dump, no labels, no purity statistics, no candidate list, and was barred from the repository

results.fires_when: for <var> in <iterable>: loop header; trial-division range() loops
results.evidence: 8/12 chunk_texts start with 'for'; across the other 120 sampled firings only ONE does

results.fires_when: chunks containing a bare `else:` / branch tail followed by an assignment
results.evidence: 3/12 contain `else:` with a following assignment; several more are branch tails

results.fires_when: line start with an indentation run opening a statement inside a block body
middle of a long floating-point/trig expression, cut mid-parenthesis

results.evidence: three sub-groups may be corpus redundancy rather than a rule

results.fires_when: nothing content-specific; the default/majority code, ~43% of chunks
results.evidence: 12 samples span chunk_index 1-29 with no shared lexical or syntactic feature

results.fires_when: the FIRST chunk of a file (chunk_index 0), regardless of content
results.evidence: 11/12 have chunk_index 0 with empty context_before; file_idx spacing 67 = 809/12, i.e. one firing per file; across the other 120 sampled firings none has chunk_index 0

results.fires_when: simple assignment statements; may be no better than chance
results.evidence: 9/12 contain an assignment, but assignments are very dense in this corpus

results.fires_when: no clean rule; contradictory conditional and positional signals
results.evidence: 5/12 contain a comparison conditional but the positional story does not hold

results.fires_when: no discernible content rule; second generic default code
results.evidence: samples span all chunk indices and all four problem families

summary.headline: Blind on raw source chunks, the interpreter named the top construct detector (t10 -> For, the highest position-matched lift in the table), described both BinOp codes as arithmetic expressions and one If code by its else-branch, and correctly declined to find structure in the five near-chance Call codes. Its two high-confidence calls are both content-free codes and both correct. Most notably it flagged t9 -- which has the second-highest GLOBAL lift (4.40x) and looks like the best FunctionDef detector in the codebook -- as a pure chunk-0 position marker, which is exactly what the position-matched control found (lift_pos = 1.00x). It reached that from raw firings alone, with no statistics.
